title: Redzone All the Time / The Choe–Chang Method / Men Evolution
summary: Chapter 15 moves from Mangchi's damaged opening performance into a long argument about work, management, friendship and male intimacy. Steve Lee's prior job-retention wrestling returns immediately: he says he does not want to wrestle, asks whether he has to, receives only a same-day assurance and reports a strained back. Guest David Chang then helps construct the joking but materially consequential ‘Choe–Chang Method’: stricter restaurant-style labor, reduced or performance-dependent pay, body-fat targets, humiliation and coercive ‘tiger dad’ rhetoric. The record preserves both the group's later language of incentives and the underlying power facts. A proposed 5% male body-fat target is the low-reference boundary identified in sports-medicine guidance, not a routine wellness goal or proof of fight readiness. Critter's Burning Man report combines direct observation, secondhand sex/drug stories, jokes and racialized generalizations. Official Burning Man material confirms MOOP means Matter Out of Place and ties it to Leave No Trace, but does not validate the episode's more sensational hearsay. A Wyoming fly-fishing story credits the guide's extensive labor and distinguishes relaxation from contested wildlife claims: Grand Teton identifies rainbow trout as nonnative, yet its current rules do not impose a universal kill requirement, so the episode's claim needs exact water and historical regulation before reuse. The episode repeatedly discusses private women, intimate images and paid sex. Bill Poon's autonomy objection—do not bargain over another person's body—remains alongside David's contrary account; no private person becomes searchable. A Help Steve Lee donation button reportedly raised a few hundred dollars, but no ledger is verified and IRS guidance says gifts to a specific individual are not deductible charitable contributions merely because a button calls them donations. The compensation proposal ties Steve's earnings to donations, creative output and body composition while joking about breaking him down, waterboarding and forced restaurant labor. These are workplace and health-power signals, not a self-improvement recipe. A woman participant later refuses wrestling three times. Media discussion connects the show's deliberately underprepared style to Howard Stern, VICE, Charlie Rose and a proposed Choe–Chang company; career, restaurant, church-video and Emmy claims remain attributed unless independently verified. The music-business section ranges through Mangchi, Igloo Hong Records, Money Mark, Dan the Automator, Nosaj Thing, U2/Apple and Taylor Swift, while David Chang describes wanting food with mass-cultural reach rather than only elite acclaim. The closing trivia/contact sequence is retained in full because post-hoc laughter does not erase chronology: a body owner says he does not want anal-area smelling; another participant refuses; a charity alternative is proposed; wrestling is refused; pressure and clothing instructions continue; the body owner says stop, no, that he is afraid and wants out; apparent contact follows. Video is required before describing the physical act. No line-level speaker names publish because no held-out acoustic identity windows have passed validation.
